scene.note: server.js runs on the shed laptop and answers anyone who opens its address with the free plots, read from the list Rhiannon keeps.

steps.note: The server starts, takes its port from the setting, listens, and says where.
Someone at the gate opens the address, and a request reaches the server.
The server reads the plot list as it is right now, Rhiannon's latest changes included.
It ends the answer with the free plots as its body, and the phone shows them.
A request comes in, as before.
If the plot list can be read, the answer is a success and says it is plain text.
If it cannot, the server catches the error and answers with a failure status and one plain line.
Either way the server keeps running for the next visitor.
The server reads the port setting, and uses a default when it is missing or empty.
A setting that is not a port is refused in one line, before the server listens.
If another program already holds the port, the server says which port in one line and ends.
The server is answering visitors when Rhiannon presses Ctrl+C on the laptop.
A listener for the signal closes the server instead of ending the script on the spot.
Once the last answer has gone, it says it has stopped, and the script ends by itself.
